help.title: Help Center
help.subtitle: A short guide to running your training on the platform: build a group, open a contest, add problems, then grade what your students submit.

group.title: Create a group
group.summary: A group is your class: the students you train together.
actions: Open {{myGroups}} from the sidebar.
Click {{createGroup}}.
Enter the group title and a short description of its goals.
Under {{members}}, pick the students. Search by name or email, or select all.
Click {{createGroup}} to save. The new group appears in your list.
group.adminNote: As an admin, you also choose the trainer who will run the group.
group.tip: You can add or remove students at any time with the {{membersButton}} button on the group card.

shots.list: Your groups, with the Create Group button

contest.title: Create a contest
contest.summary: A contest is a timed set of problems for one group.
actions: On the group card, click {{view}} to open the group.
In the {{contestsTab}} tab, click {{createContest}}.
Enter the contest title and choose its difficulty.
Set the start and end date and time. The end must be after the start.
Click {{submit}}. Every student in the group can now see the contest.
contest.tip: You can also create contests from {{contestsPage}} in the sidebar. There you choose which group the contest belongs to.

problems.title: Add problems
problems.summary: Problems are the questions your students solve during the contest.
actions: On the contest card, click {{problems}}.
Click {{addProblem}}.
Write the title, category and the problem statement.
Optionally add constraints, worked examples and an image.
Choose the difficulty and the points (1 to 1000). The points are the highest score a student can get.
Click {{createProblem}}. Repeat for each problem in the contest.
problems.tip: Problems can be edited or removed until the contest ends. After that the contest is locked.

grade.title: Grade student solutions
grade.summary: Review each answer, give a score and leave feedback.
actions: Open the contest's problems (see step 3).
Click a problem's name to open {{progress}}. It shows who submitted and who is still pending.
Next to a student, click {{viewSolution}}.
Read the solution, enter a score between 0 and the problem's points, and add feedback if you like.
Click {{markAsDone}}. The student sees the score and your feedback.
grade.tip: Grading opens once the contest has ended. Before that you can read submissions, but not score them.
